title: Adaptive calibration sampling and tail-latency matrix for FP8/INT8 quant variants
creator: Leo Armstrong
description: Goal: Produce an experiment and validation harness that measures tail-latency and throughput interactions for FP8 and INT8 quantized model profiles under realistic mixed-batching and long-context workloads, while improving calibration sample selection to reduce accuracy drift.
background: We have a family of quantization profiles (per-channel FP8, per-layer INT8 symmetric/asymmetric) that show good average throughput gains but exhibit variable tail-latency behavior in production when combined with KV-cache warmup and mixed-burst arrival patterns. Previous benchmarking focused on steady-state throughput over fixed batch sizes and uniformly sampled sequences; this ticket builds a matrix combining microburst patterns, kv-cache warmup phases, and stratified calibration samples to understand and mitigate tail regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook and reproducible benchmark harness committed to repo with clear invocation flags for: profile, backend device, batch policy, kv-cache state, and arrival pattern
End-to-end latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) and tokens/sec reported for all matrix cells and uploaded to the dashboard
Calibration sampling change (stratified prompt buckets) implemented and evaluated; show reduction in accuracy regression compared to baseline sampling on held-out prompts
Accuracy validation: embedding cosine and n-gram overlap metrics for quantized vs baseline FP16/FP32 available; delta thresholds documented and within agreed limits for accepted profiles

Recommendations documented: which profiles and batching configs are safe for long-context/production, with rollback criteria and mitigation steps (fallback to higher-precision profile or warm-start cache).
experiment_matrix: Hardware: A100-80GB, H100-80GB (single-GPU), cloud-like networking latency simulated
Models: base-13b and base-70b checkpoints (sharded where applicable)
Profiles: FP16 baseline, FP8 (per-channel), INT8 (per-layer symmetric), INT8 (per-layer asymmetric)
Batching policies: static batching (sizes 1/4/8), dynamic continuous batching (target latency 100ms), and mixed-priority batching (PL1/PL2 routes)
KV-cache states: cold (no cache), warm (prefix cached for 128 tokens), hot (full prefix cached for 512 tokens)
Sequence lengths: short (64), medium (512), long (2048), extended (8192)
Arrival patterns: steady QPS, bursty microbursts (poisson with 95th percentile bursts), adversarial bursts (sustained spike for 30s), and tail-triggered spikes (background + sudden large request)
Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec, cost-per-token estimate (relative), memory high-water mark, kernel fallback counts, kv-cache hit ratio, calibration-induced accuracy delta
calibration_workflow: Stratified prompt sampling: partition calibration corpus into buckets by token-length, prompt-construction type (instruction/QA/dialog), domain (finance/health/general), and sampling weight each bucket proportional to observed production frequency
Per-layer sensitivity sweep: run calibration candidates with per-layer quant thresholds and collect activation histograms; store artifacts with deterministic seeds
Automatic outlier clipping heuristics: detect layers with heavy-tailed activations and enable per-layer clip scaling or mixed-precision fallback
Calibration artifacts: store candidate calibration tables + metadata (seed, prompt-bucket, hw profile) in /artifacts/quant-calib/ for reproducibility
Calibration CI: lightweight nightly run comparing top-N calibration candidates on a small held-out adversarial set to detect drift before promotion
accuracy_validation: Reference: FP16 baseline outputs and embedding vectors from the same seed set
Text similarity: ROUGE-L and BLEU where applicable, and edit-distance for structured outputs
Embedding similarity: cosine threshold (default >= 0.995 for acceptable), report distribution and fraction below 0.99
Behavioral tests: set of functional assertions (e.g., math answers, code-generation canonical outputs) with strict pass/fail
Adversarial prompts: intentionally edge-case prompts (long prefix, ambiguous instructions, domain jargon) to surface calibration brittleness
Acceptance thresholds: mean metric delta <= 1.5% for ROUGE, <= 0.5% drop for embedding cosine mean; no regression in critical functional tests
results_placeholder: (To be filled) Commit stable harness and initial run artifacts. Expect p99 variance in some INT8/asym cells; follow-up will tune per-layer clipping and batching policy to reduce regressions.
notes_or_risks: INT8 asym profiles may require per-layer special-casing for transformer MLP layers; this could increase runtime branching and reduce throughput gains
KV-cache warmup creates a non-linear latency surface — small bursts during cold cache can disproportionately affect p99
